# PR #2301: Patch: the Almanac and the other card grids render fast again

Closes #2266

## What changed

`apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/PoolGrid.tsx` is the only source file touched. The same file serves the Almanac and the deck builder's pool. Three parts:

- **Memoized cards.** `PoolCard = memo(PoolItem, samePoolItem)` compares each card's deck share field by field. `itemDeck` builds a fresh object on every render, so the default shallow compare would never match. A filter, sort, ownership or deck change therefore re-renders only the cards it changes.
- **Stable handlers.** The grid hands its cards handlers that never change and call the screen's latest props through a ref. DeckEditor's `add` changes with every card the deck takes, so without this the memo would be useless or the handlers stale.
- **Staged mount.** `POOL_FIRST_CARDS = 48` cards are drawn at once. The rest come in a `useDeferredValue` background render, which yields to input. A pool that shrinks or reorders is drawn at once, because deferring a narrowing search made it slower (87–94 ms against 42–46 ms in the planner's measurement).

R2098000 is untouched. The planner built and measured delegated stateless terms and found no change, so `TermTip.tsx` stays as it is.

## Review finding (pass 2): it held

Reproduced in code: the staged render showed `deferred`, the previous pool's first cards, whenever the new pool was longer. A filter landing mid-render could draw cards that fail it while the count already showed the new number. `33-almanac.cy.ts` can hit this, since its `.each` over cost words does not retry.

**Fix:** a growing pool now draws `ids.slice(0, deferred.length)`, the new pool's own first cards. It stays staged, and it never draws a card the pool does not hold.

**Test:** the new test `a pool that grows into other cards never draws a card the pool does not hold` goes from 10 cards to 60 different ones and checks every commit. I put the old `deferred : ids` expression back and the test failed. With the fix it passes.

**Side effect, and a test change to match:** when a pool grows and also reorders, a card the new order puts past the first `deferred.length` is unmounted and then mounted anew. It does not keep its old instance, so it re-renders. I changed the first render-count test's reorder step to `["core-008","core-002","core-004"]`, where the two cards that stay keep their place, and added a comment. I did not weaken the assertion: only `core-004` renders.

## Decisions

- `shown` is the new pool's first `deferred.length` ids rather than a filter of the old pool's cards. The alternatives are worse: filtering the old cards could show nothing for disjoint pools.
- `SLOW_GRID` stays in `almanac.test.tsx` and `almanac-preview.test.tsx`. Under jsdom, `act` flushes the background render, so each render still mounts every face. The planner measured those tests at 3.6–4.5 s standalone against vitest's 5 s default, so removing the timeouts would be flaky.
- Row virtualization and cheaper faces would be needed to match the 481-card baseline on the time to draw the whole grid and on the scroll p95. That belongs in a follow-up issue. The first cards, filter changes and detail opens do beat the baseline in the planner's table.

## Tested

I ran `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/deckbuilder src/routes/almanac.test.tsx src/routes/almanac-preview.test.tsx src/cards/TermTip.test.tsx`: 16 files, 451 tests, all passed. `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` is clean. eslint on `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder` is clean.

I did not run the full web suite or the e2e specs this pass, and I did not re-measure the production build, so the planner's numbers (baseline 9be40af, main, and this plan) are the only ones I have. `src/cards/textLimit.test.ts` "B15 R1017000 the premise…" fails on unchanged main (traininggrounds-039 has no short form). It is not caused by this change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### Adversarial review

Approved on round 2 of 3.

Notes the reviewer left (not blocking):

- `task`: Two parts of the acceptance are not fully met. The whole grid takes longer to be in the DOM than on the baseline and on main, and the scroll p95 is worse than the baseline. The PR's numbers also come from the planner's build of the earlier `shown = deferred` version, not from this code.
- `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/PoolGrid.tsx:365`: When a pool grows, the first draw shows the new pool's first `deferred.length` ids. Cards the old pool showed beyond that point are unmounted and then mounted again, and cards new to that range mount during the first draw. Widening from a large filter can therefore do more blocking work than the planner measured.
- `apps/web/src/routes/almanac.test.tsx`: `SLOW_GRID` stays in both Almanac tests, and the PR explains why instead of removing it, which the issue allows.

| web tests (`sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm exec vitest run --project web --changed origin/main --exclude '**/src/audio/**' --exclude '**/src/fx/**' --exclude '**/src/cards/art/convention.test.ts'`) | pass | 418s |

# #2266: Patch: the Almanac and the other card grids render fast again
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

## What happens

`/almanac` has become noticeably slow to open, scroll and filter after the last few days' patches. The slowness probably reaches the other places that draw many card faces too: the deck builder's pool (the same `PoolGrid`), the hand and board, pile dialogs and inspect lists.

Nobody has profiled it yet. These are the likely causes, all from reading the code on `main` (795c3f2):

1. **#2145 (R2098000) made every keyword on every face a live React component.** `PoolGrid.tsx` wraps each face in `<TermTips>`, so each `cf-term` in a card's text renders `LiveTerm` (`cards/TermTip.tsx`). Each one has a `useId`, a `useState`, four refs, a cleanup `useEffect`, a `useLayoutEffect` and seven pointer, focus and click handlers. With about 710 faces and several keywords per face, that adds up to thousands of stateful components in one grid, mostly for cards no one hovers over. #2145 also added `TermTips` to `game/Card.tsx`, `game/PileBrowser`, `cards/inspect/CardList.tsx` and `useInspectTrigger`.
2. **The grid nearly doubled.** The Stinkyscape release (#2178) took the Almanac to a 710-entry grid. That release's own description says it gave `almanac-preview.test.tsx` the 30 s grid timeout `almanac.test.tsx` already had. #263 tuned the first layout for 318 faces (`deckbuilder.css`, the `.db-card-face` comment). `content-visibility: auto` skips layout and paint of off-screen faces, but React still mounts and reconciles every `PoolItem`.
3. **Every item has its own per-card overhead.** Each `PoolItem` gets an `AsOwnCopy` (two context providers, R1956000), a `faceModel` memo, `useFullArt`, `useOwnCopy`, `useInspectTrigger` with its overlay, and `useLocale`. Any change to the filter, sort, win rates or ownership re-renders all ~710 items, because `PoolItem` is not memoized and gets a fresh `deck` object each render from `itemDeck(...)`.
4. Possibly also the CSS from #2221 (type scale) and #2188 (`text-wrap: balance`, tabular numbers), if those selectors reach the card faces' text. `text-wrap: balance` on hundreds of faces makes layout cost more, and `fit.ts` text fitting re-runs on top of it.

Measure before changing anything, and fix what the profile shows. Don't treat this list as settled.

## What should happen

The Almanac should open, scroll and filter at least as fast as it did before #2145 and #2178. Every rule the recent patches added has to keep working:

- R2098000: hovering or long-pressing a keyword shows its rule, and in control mode the term is a tab stop with `role="tooltip"` and `aria-describedby`.
- R1956000: the signed-in viewer's own copies show their cosmetics.
- R1383: the "New" ribbon.
- R630 / R654: the read-only grid and the detail view's statistics.

## What to change (guidance, not a prescription)

- **Profile first.** Use a production build (`pnpm --dir apps/web build && pnpm --dir apps/web exec vite preview`) with Chromium's Performance panel or React Profiler, on `/almanac`, on `main`, and on the commit just before e653835 (#2145) for a baseline. Record the time to first render of the grid, the scripting time of a filter change, and frame times while scrolling. Put the numbers in the PR.
- **Make terms cheap by default.** Faces in a grid could print terms as plain `<strong class="cf-term" data-term data-tip>` and handle hover and long-press with one delegated listener per surface (for example on `TermTips` or the grid's `section`). Only the term being hovered or pressed would then mount the tooltip state. `startsOnTermTip` already finds terms by selector, so delegation fits how the module works. Keep R2098000's behaviour and its tests (`TermTip.test.tsx`, the `PoolGrid`, `Card` and `PileBrowser` cases) green.
- **Stop re-rendering the whole grid.** Memoize `PoolItem` with stable props: keep `itemDeck`'s result stable for each card, or pass its fields as primitives. Then a filter, sort or ownership change only re-renders the cards it affects.
- If the profile still shows the grid mount as the cost, consider mounting cards in chunks or virtualizing the rows. That must keep the e2e and unit specs that look up `card-pool-<id>` working, and keep the accessible names.
- Apply the same fixes wherever else #2145 put `TermTips` and the profile shows a cost: the hand and board, `PileBrowser`, and `CardList`.
- Any new threshold (chunk size, delay) is a named constant in `cards/constants.ts` or the module's own constants (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

    while (!test()) { const now = await frame(); longest = Math.max(longest, now - last); last = now; }
    return [performance.now() - start, longest];
  };
  const runs = { openFirst: [], openWhole: [], openLongest: [], narrowLongest: [], clearFirst: [], clearWhole: [], clearLongest: [], detail: [] };
